brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Dozeline, the iOS and Android wind-down and sleep journal app in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm, warm, not clinical, no moons or stars cliché. The app icon must be recognisable on a home screen at small sizes. English and Turkish markets.

claim.notes: No concept passed: the critic gave sketch pick 'none' to all three directions in two review rounds, so all were rejected and nothing was developed, finalized or exported.

concepts.title: Evening Handover
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 two parallelograms, a fast-forward or chevron arrow; s7 the letter L; s8 the letter Z, the Zzz sleep cliché; s9 a folded page corner or dog-ear (a struck product-object cliché) plus a play/forward arrow. The two-tone ribbon carries none of it: at 16 px they are flat brown and yellow polygons. Different move: the bookmark-handover idea needs a silhouette that reads as a bookmark resting in something (a journal spine, a pillow edge) without letters or arrows; otherwise retire the concept.

concepts.title: Horizon D
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a D on an underline (initial plus bar, stock monogram); s3 an open D/backwards c with a dot, an eye or a Pac-Man; s4 a cake or a head on a pillow emoji; s5 a bowl/eye with a lid, a sunrise; s6 a lowercase d or mirrored J; s7 a bib or half-disc; s8 a U or magnet; s9 a tipped A or a flag. Letter readings dominate, and the ones that do not read as a letter read as a different object. Different move: drop the D-as-container; if the initial stays, it needs one feature that is not a cut, offset or sag of the letter, and that feature must be the first thing a stranger sees.

concepts.title: Settling Steps
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a left-aligned text/list icon (UI); s3 a staircase/step chart; s6 a backslash or tilde swoosh, generic; s7 a cursive e or awareness-ribbon loop, mushy at 16 px; s8 a smiley mouth or a ball in a cup (closest, but the sinking-sun-in-valley reading is a sunset cliché next door to the banned moon); s9 a hook or pigtail curl, no eyelid reading. None would reach distinctiveness 7. Different move: stop drawing a single line doing a gesture; find one ownable silhouette with a specific feature (an asymmetric weight, a notch, a closed counter) that a stranger reads as one thing at 16 px, and test the reading cold before captioning it.
